highlights_headline: The upcoming SkiaSharp 4.159.0 release adds custom GPU mesh drawing and improves rendering reliability.
highlights_body: Build meshes with SkSL vertex and fragment programs, uniforms, and child effects. Other changes correct iOS and tvOS device frameworks and bring upstream fixes for glyph rendering, image-filter caching, and Vulkan allocation failures.

bullets.detail: SKMeshSpecification, mesh builders, vertex and index buffers, and SKCanvas.DrawMesh expose SkSL-based custom mesh drawing. Indexed meshes use 16-bit indices; buffers can be CPU-backed or Ganesh GPU-backed. Drawing requires a GPU-backed surface: raster canvases do not draw meshes.

bullets.lead: Correct iOS and tvOS device frameworks
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp device frameworks now contain only arm64 device binaries and matching platform metadata, avoiding App Store validation failures caused by embedded simulator slices. Simulator frameworks and their x86_64 and arm64 symbols remain available.

An upstream Skia m159 fix makes image-filter cache equality consistent with hashing for signed zero, matrix type-mask state, and subnormal values, correcting cache behavior without changing package or native ABI versions.

Upstream fixes handle stateful font scalers whose repeated glyph loads produce different paths, mask formats, or bounds. Rendering uses the reloaded glyph, clears incompatible masks instead of overflowing sub-byte rows, and correctly copies clipped emboss masks.

Ganesh and Graphite abandon descriptor pools after host or device out-of-memory allocation errors on Imagination drivers, avoiding a driver failure during pool destruction. Graphite also prevents further allocation from the abandoned pool; the workaround is limited to this vendor and these errors.

contributor_summaries.kdpkke: Corrected iOS and tvOS device-framework binaries and metadata while preserving simulator support
